title: RNA coIP from gradients
author: Motoko Tanaka
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.k74czqw
materials: RNA co-­‐Immunoprecipitation By Motoko Tanaka and Brook Barajas in Jaisri Lingappa’s Laboratory, October 2017 Day 0: Plate Cells (for cos-­‐1 cells, split cell ~8hr before transfection) -­‐ COS-­‐1 cells: 6e5 cells/poly lysine-­‐coated 60m plate; 293T: 2e6 cells/60mm plate. -­‐ Use 4% lysate for TCL IP (=4.72x10^4 cell equivalent, 25 µL out of 620.5 µL lysate) Day 0: Transfect Cells 8 hours after plating cells, transfect each plate with desired plasmid(s). Before starting: • Label 1 1.5 mL Eppies per sample. • Thaw DNA at 55˚C in Thermomixer and rotate at >1000 RPM for 15 minutes to resuspend. • Thaw PEI (MANUFACTURER, CATALOGUE NUMBER) at 55˚C in Thermomixer and rotate at >1000 RPM for 15 minutes to resuspend. 1. For each transfection condition, dilute DNA in 500 µL pre-­‐warmed, serum-­‐free medium. 2. Let sit 5 minutes at room temperature (RT). 3. Add 20 µL of pre-­‐warmed PEI (more than 15min at 55˚C) to DNA/ serum-­‐media, incubate at RT 15 minutes. 4. Change media on cells to 3 mL of transfection media. 5. Add transfection mix dropwise to cells while gently rocking the plate. Day 1: Change media (when you culture cells more than 24 hrs after transfection) Before starting: • Warm PBS + MgCl2/CaCl2 • Warm culture media (for 293Ts and Cos-­‐1, 500 mLs DMEM + 10% FBS + 5 mLs penicillin/streptomycin) ~14 hours post transfection, rinse cells twice with 3 mL warmed PBS containing CaCl2 and MgCl2 to remove untransfected DNA, then add 3.5 mL fresh media. Day 2: HARVEST (1xNMPH harvest), Gradient fractionation, IPs Harvest lysate in NMPH (dissociating ribosomes and releasing the nascent chain): Before starting: • Label and pre-­‐chill 3 1.5 mL Eppie tubes per sample. • Pre-­‐chill benchtop Allegra centrifuge to 4˚C. • Pre-­‐chill a microcentrifuge to 4˚C. • Pre-­‐chill 1 mL syringes with 20 gauge needles attached. • Prepare a “cell scraper” – an aspirator pipette with a rubber policeman scraper at the end. • Thaw an aliquot of Puromycin (need 26.5 µL for each sample) – Puromycin should not undergo multiple freeze-­‐thaw cycles. • Make sure you have 144 µL of 2M KCl NN+M (high salt) per sample, keep chilled. 1. Rinse cells with 3mL ice-­‐cold PBS containing CaCl2 and MgCl2 twice to remove untransfected DNA.

6. Proceeding in the same sample order, go back and aspirate any liquid that has collected after the first aspiration. 7. Remove the magnet from the tube holder and place holder with tubes on the lidless grey ice tray. Detergent washes: 8. Using an RNase-­‐free repeater, add 1 mL cold IP wash buffer to each tube (opening four tubes at a time, then recapping). 9. Invert tubes in holder to thoroughly resuspend beads, then rotate at RT for 1 minute. 10. Place tubes back in the magnet and allow beads to pellet completely. 11. Invert once to collect remaining beads from the cap and allow to pellet again. 12. Aspirate off supernatant from the tube and cap. 13. Proceeding in the same sample order, go back and aspirate any liquid that has collected after the first aspiration. 14. Repeat three more times for a total of four washes. Non-­‐detergent wash (proteinase K compatible = no EDTA): 15. Using a filter tip on a P1000 pipetman, add 1 mL of cold non-­‐detergent wash buffer to each tube (again opening four tubes at a time, then recapping). 16. Invert tubes in holder to thoroughly resuspend beads, then rotate at RT for 1 minute. 17. Place tubes in the magnet and allow beads to pellet completely. 18. Invert once to collect remaining beads from the cap and allow to pellet again. 19. Aspirate off supernatant from the tube and cap. 20. Proceeding in the same sample order, go back and aspirate any liquid that has collected after the first aspiration. 21. Place samples back in the ice tray with the tube-­‐holder lid and proceed with washing the next set of 16 samples. Proteinase K reaction and TRIZOL: Before starting: • Make up 1.5 mL Eppie tubes for TCL and VLP from each sample. • Make up non-­‐detergent 1x NN buffer (see end of protocol). • Obtain 1 mL Trizol (Ambion, cat# 15590026) for each sample (make an aliquot of the needed volume + 10%, being careful not to draw from the bottom of the bottle). • Preheat RNA bench heat-­‐block or water bath to 55˚C. • Obtain 20 mg/mL Proteinase K (Sigma P4850). 1. Make up Proteinase K elution buffer To make 1 ml (for approx. 10 samples): 975 µL of non-­‐detergent 1x NN (see end of protocol) 15 µL Proteinase K 10 µL 10% SDS 2. Add elution buffer to samples: a. Gradient IPs: remove last wash and add 100 µL proteinase K elution buffer to beads. b. Gradient IP input: Take 12 µL from gradient fractions 1-­‐18 and 28 or 18 µL from combined gradient fractions 19-­‐21, 22-­‐24, 25-­‐27 (10% gradient IP input) c. TCL input: take 2.5 µL of TCL (10% TCL IP input) 3. Add proteinase K elution buffer to equal 100 µL. 4. Incubate at 55˚C for 30 minutes. 5. Add 1 ml TRIZOL. Invert to mix well and incubate at RT for 5 minutes.

-­‐ Store at -­‐80C if stopping. If you want to stop the experiment, stop at this point. RNA is not stable in isopropanol. Next stop point is the end of cDNA reaction. Day 3: RNA isolation and Reverse Transcription reaction RNA isolation with TRIZOL: Before starting RNA isolation and DNAse treatment: • Obtain 5 µL Glycoblue (Invitrogen AM9515 or AM9516) per sample. • Obtain 100 µL BCP (BP 151 phase separation reagent, Molecular Research Center, CATALOGUE NUMBER) per sample. • Prepare 0.7 mL of ice cold isopropanol per sample (store at -­‐20˚C until ready for use). • Prepare 1 mL of ice cold 75% ethanol per sample with PCR grade or DEPC-­‐treated water (store at -­‐20˚C until ready for use). • Prepare 51 µL of 1xDNase buffer (Invitrogen cat# 18068-­‐015, prepare with DEPC water) containing 1:1000 RNaseOut and 2U (1 µL) DNase (Invitrogen cat# 18068-­‐015) per sample. • Heat a clean-­‐room heat block or water bath to 25˚C. • Heat a clean-­‐room heat block or water bath to 65˚C. • Obtain 1.5 µL of 25mM EDTA per sample. • Pre-­‐chill an RNA-­‐designated centrifuge. • Clean benchtop, Pipetmen, and all equipment with RNase-­‐ZAP (MANUFACTURER, CATALOGUE NUMBER) or similar reagent. 1. If samples are frozen, thaw at room temperature and set on ice. Invert many times to promote lysis of material. 2. Spin down briefly to collect inverted liquid. 3. Add 75 μg of glycoblue (5 µL) and mix well by inverting tube. 4. Spin down briefly to collect inverted liquid. 5. Add 100 µL of BCP. 6. Vortex for 10-­‐15 seconds until emulsion forms, repeat 2 times. 7. Let sit on ice for 2-­‐3 minutes. 8. Spin 12,000xg 15 minutes at 4˚C in chilled RNA-­‐designated microcentrifuge. 9. While tubes are spinning, for each sample transfer 0.7 mL of ice cold isopropanol to a fresh labeled tube. Set tubes on ice. 10. With a 1 mL Pipetman, transfer ~0.6 mL of the aqueous phase from the spun sample directly to the tube with the isopropanol. Keep all samples on ice. 11. Mix well by inverting at least 5 times. 12. Transfer to -­‐20˚C for at least 1 hour. 13. Spin at full-­‐speed (14K RPM) for 30 minutes in cold room or in chilled benchtop centrifuge, then carefully use a 1 mL pipette to remove the supernatant without touching the pellet (tip the tube). 14. Wash pellet with 1 mL of 75% ice cold EtOH by inverting several times. 15. Spin full speed (14K RPM) for 10 minutes in chilled benchtop centrifuge. 16. Aspirate most of the EtOH. 17. Spin full speed (14K RPM) for 1 minute in chilled benchtop centrifuge, then pipet to remove the remaining EtOH (with P200). 18. MOVE samples to clean room: everything will be in a clean room or clean area after this

steps.title: Prepare Cell Lysate
steps.instruction: Lysis and shearing of cells to prepare the starting material.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL of 1x Lysis Buffer NN+M (supplemented with 1:100 Protease Inhibitor and 1:1000 RNaseOUT) per plate.
Scrape lysate and transfer to a chilled tube.
Shear lysed cells 20 times through a chilled 20-gauge needle.
Centrifuge at 1000 RPM for 10 minutes at 4°C in a tabletop Allegra; transfer supernatant to a new tube.
Centrifuge supernatant at 14k RPM for 1 minute at 4°C in a microcentrifuge.
Transfer 450 µL of the resulting lysate to a new tube.

steps.title: Puromycin Treatment
steps.instruction: Treat lysate with puromycin and high salt to isolate specific complexes.

substeps.instruction: Warm lysate and Puromycin for 5 minutes at 26°C.
Add 26.5 µL Puromycin (18mM stock) to 450 µL of lysate to reach a final concentration of 1mM.
Incubate for 10 minutes at 26°C.
Add 144 µL 2M high salt NN+M to reach a final concentration of 0.5M KCl (final volume 620.5 µL).
Incubate for 10 minutes at 26°C.
Place tubes on ice for at least 10 minutes.
Centrifuge at max speed for 1 minute in a 4°C microcentrifuge.

steps.title: Sucrose Gradient Separation
steps.instruction: Separate complexes using either a 10-80% or 5-30% sucrose gradient.

substeps.instruction: For Gradient A (10-80%): Prepare 7 layers of 675 µL each (10/15/40/50/60/70/80% w/v sucrose in 1x buffer). Load 200 µL lysate on top. Centrifuge at 45K rpm for 45 min at 4°C. Fractionate into 175 µL x ~27 fractions plus pellet (fraction 28).

For Gradient B (5-30%): Prepare 6 layers of 790 µL each (5/10/15/20/25/30% w/v sucrose in 1x buffer). Load 200 µL lysate on top. Centrifuge at 45K rpm for 90 min at 4°C. Fractionate into 240 µL x ~20 or 480 µL x ~10 fractions.

steps.title: Prepare IP Reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare buffers, beads, and antibodies before starting the immunoprecipitation.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1x NN IP wash buffer plus detergent.
Prepare Protein G Dynal beads: Aliquot 20 µL bead slurry per IP, wash three times with 1mL 1x NN IP wash buffer plus detergent, and keep on ice.
Prepare antibody plus IP buffer master mixes.
Ensure filter tips are used for all pipetting.

steps.title: Perform Immunoprecipitation (IP)
steps.instruction: Carry out IP for gradient fractions or total cell lysate (TCL).

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL IP buffer/antibody to a 1.5 mL Eppie tube on ice.
Add lysate: 120 µL for Gradient A fractions 1-18 or Gradient B; 180 µL for combined Gradient A fractions (19-21, 22-24, 25-27); or 25 µL for TCL.
Add 260 µL of 1xNN buffer plus detergent (resulting in 360 µL total buffer).
Incubate on ice for 30 minutes.
Add 20 µL IP beads.
Rotate on an RNase-free rotor for 1 hour at 4°C.

steps.title: IP Washing and RNA Recovery
steps.instruction: Wash the IP complexes and recover the RNA pellet.

substeps.instruction: Remove tubes from rotator and place on ice in a rack with a tube-holder lid.
Process samples in order: Non-Immunes (NI), then Immunes (I), then TCL IPs to minimize contamination.
Place tubes in an RNase-free magnet to pellet beads; invert to collect beads from cap and pellet again.
Aspirate supernatant from tube and cap (change aspirator tip when switching sample types).
Allow RNA pellets to dry with open lids for ~3 minutes, closing the tube as they dry to prevent over-drying.

steps.title: DNase I Treatment
steps.instruction: Remove contaminating DNA from the RNA pellet.

substeps.instruction: Add 51 µL of 1x DNase buffer (DEPC water) containing 1:1000 RNaseOut and 2U DNase (1 µL) by sliding it down the sidewall onto the pellet.
Tap to resuspend and spin down briefly.
Mix by pipetting 5 times, running the liquid over the sidewall to ensure full resuspension.
Incubate at 25°C for 15 minutes.
Add 1.5 µL of 25mM EDTA, mix, and spin.
Heat at 65°C for 10 minutes to inactivate DNase I.

steps.title: cDNA Synthesis (RT Reaction)
steps.instruction: Convert recovered RNA into cDNA using the iScript Advanced cDNA synthesis kit.

substeps.instruction: Prepare +RT master mix: 10 µL PCR grade H2O, 4 µL 5X Script reaction mix, and 1 µL 20X RT enzyme mix.
Aliquot 15 µL master mix per sample and add 5 µL RNA (Total 20 µL).
Prepare -RNA control: 15 µL master mix + 5 µL DEPC H2O.
Prepare -RT controls: 15 µL PCR grade H2O + 5 µL RNA.
Incubate samples at 42°C for 30 minutes in a water bath.
Incubate samples at 85°C for 5 minutes in a heat block.
Dilute cDNA 1:3 by adding 51 µL DEPC H2O to 17 µL cDNA.

steps.title: qPCR Setup and Execution
steps.instruction: Quantify the target RNA using qPCR with a standard curve.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 10 µM oligo mix (dilute 200 µM forward and reverse oligos 1:1).
Prepare standard curve outside clean room: 1:10 dilutions from 1e1 to 1e8 copies/2 µL (add 5 µL dilution to 45 µL DEPC water).
Prepare qPCR mix: 9.75 µL DEPC water, 12.5 µL 2xSYBR, and 0.75 µL 10µM oligo mix.
Set up duplicate reactions in Eppies, then aliquot to a 96-well plate.
Add 2 µL of 1:3 diluted cDNA to sample wells and 2 µL of standards to standard wells.
Seal plate with foil and centrifuge briefly at 500 RPM.
Run qPCR program: 95°C (30s), then 35 cycles of [95°C (15s), 60°C (15s), 72°C (30s + 10s collection)], followed by 55°C (1 min) and 55°C Tm measurement.
